tickets.question_sent: E-04 keeps coming up overnight when the drive is just sat there not running anything. Measured the incoming supply at 535 V between phases. Is that the problem?
tickets.rejected_answer:
E-04 is a DC bus overvoltage fault that occurs when the DC bus voltage inside the VX-200 rises above 800 V DC while the drive is stopped or running at steady frequency.

Your incoming supply of 535 V between phases is not the direct cause. The DC bus voltage is derived from the AC supply through the drive's rectifier. With a 400 V supply the DC bus is at about 565 V DC, so your higher incoming voltage would result in a proportionally higher DC bus voltage, but this alone would not typically cause an 800 V trip at standstill.

E-04 at standstill suggests either:
- An external voltage source is feeding back into the drive (for example from regenerative braking or another drive on the same bus)
- A fault in the drive's power supply or DC bus circuit

Since this happens overnight when nothing is running, check for:
1. Other equipment on the same supply that might be feeding voltage back
2. Any external power sources connected to the motor or drive terminals

Isolate the drive, wait 5 minutes, then inspect the motor cable and the U, V, W terminals for damage or loose connections that could allow external voltage injection.

tickets.question_sent: Drive in a warm panel keeps tripping mid afternoon on the heatsink overtemp fault and it wont reset straight away. Fins look pretty clogged with dust. Why wont it reset and whats the proper way to clean it out?

citations.title: E-07 Drive overtemperature (heatsink)
Cleaning the heatsink and air vents
Replacing the cooling fan

tickets.answer:
The fault won't reset straight away because the heatsink is still hot. The drive needs time to cool down before the fault can be cleared.

To clean the heatsink and air vents:

1. Stop the motor and isolate the supply.
2. Wait 5 minutes for the DC bus to discharge.
3. Let the heatsink cool completely.
4. Clean the heatsink fins and air vents to remove the dust.

Clean the VX-200 every 6 months, or more often in dusty locations.

Why the fault is occurring:

The heatsink fins and air vents are blocked with dust, which reduces cooling. The drive gives its full rating from −10 °C to +40 °C and must be derated between 40 °C and 50 °C. In a warm panel, the combination of high ambient temperature and blocked cooling fins causes the drive to overheat mid afternoon.

To prevent this happening again, check your cabinet ventilation and filter are not blocked, and ensure the drive has 100 mm of free space above and below and 50 mm on each side for proper airflow.

tickets.question_sent: whats the actual difference between E-08 and E-09?? we get both on different days and nobody here knows which one means what

citations.title: E-08 Motor overload
E-09 Drive overload

tickets.answer:
E-08 protects the motor. E-09 protects the drive.

E-08 Motor overload means the motor itself is overheating or drawing too much current. E-09 Drive overload means the drive itself is overheating or reaching its current limit.

When you get E-08, let the motor cool before restarting and check for mechanical overload on the machine.

When you get E-09, wait a few minutes before restarting so the drive can recover, then check for mechanical overload and compare the drive rating with the motor nameplate.

tickets.question_sent: earth fault E-12 after washdown. ok to put the insulation tester straight on the U V W terminals of the drive to check the motor?

citations.title: E-12 Earth (ground) fault

tickets.answer:
No. Never apply an insulation tester to the drive terminals; it can damage the drive.

To check the motor after an earth fault E-12:

1. Isolate the drive and wait 5 minutes before touching any terminal.
2. Disconnect the motor cable from the U, V, W terminals of the drive.
3. Carry out an insulation resistance test on the motor and motor cable to earth (test the motor and cable, not the drive terminals).
4. Inspect the motor terminal box for moisture, dirt and loose strands.
5. Inspect the cable along its length for crushing or abrasion.

After washdown, pay particular attention to moisture in the motor terminal box.

tickets.question_sent: brand new drive, only power and motor connected, nothing on the control terminals. powers up with E-14. the little wire link that came on the terminals got taken off during wiring. related?

citations.title: E-14 External fault input active
Using the emergency stop and external fault input correctly
Pre-power-up checklist and first power-up

tickets.answer:
Yes, that is related. E-14 means the external fault input is active. By default this is digital input DI3. The input expects a normally closed contact: the circuit between DI3 and +24V must stay closed while everything is healthy. When the circuit opens, the drive stops its output, the motor coasts to a stop, the FAULT LED lights and the display flashes E-14.

The wire link that came on the terminals is the link between DI3 and +24V. The pre-power-up checklist states: "The link between DI3 and +24V is fitted, or an external fault device is wired there."

You need to refit the link between DI3 and +24V. Once you do, the E-14 fault should clear and the drive will be ready to run.

Fit cabinet ventilation if needed to keep the cabinet temperature within limits.

P-05 is the time to reach the maximum frequency in P-04, not the speed you ask for.

P-05 is the acceleration time from 0 Hz to the maximum frequency in P-04. If you set P-05 to 10 seconds, the drive takes 10 seconds to go from 0 Hz to whatever maximum frequency is set in P-04.

If you ask for a lower speed, the time is proportional. For example, with P-04 at 50.0 Hz and P-05 at 10.0 s, going from 0 to 25 Hz takes 5 seconds.

tickets.question_sent: Inherited a drive off another machine, no idea what the previous settings are. How do I wipe it back to how it left the factory, and what do I then need to set up again before running our motor?

tickets.answer:
To restore the drive to factory defaults:

1. Stop the motor.
2. Write down the present settings if they may be needed again.
3. Press MENU and go to P-15.
4. Press ENTER, set the value to 1 and press ENTER again.
5. The display shows dEF for a few seconds and then returns to the flashing frequency. P-15 returns to 0 by itself.

A restore sets every parameter from P-01 to P-54 back to its factory value. The fault history in P-55 to P-59 is kept.

After the restore, you need to set up:

1. Re-enter the motor nameplate data in P-16 to P-20.
2. Repeat the auto-tune with P-21.
3. Re-enter any other settings for your application.

Keep a written record of the parameter settings for each drive so they can be re-entered after a restore.

tickets.question_sent: How long do I have to wait after turning the supply off before I can touch the terminals? Display goes dark almost straight away so I assume its dead by then.

citations.title: Safe isolation and DC bus discharge time before working on the drive
Inspecting and re-tightening power terminals

tickets.answer:
Wait 5 minutes after switching off the supply before touching any terminal.

A dark display does not prove the drive is safe. The VX-200 contains DC bus capacitors that stay charged at a dangerous voltage after the supply is switched off. With a 400 V supply the DC bus is at about 565 V DC.

After waiting 5 minutes, confirm with a suitable voltmeter that there is no voltage on L1, L2, L3 and less than 50 V DC between DC+ and DC−.

tickets.question_sent: can we just wire the e-stop button into the external fault input and use that as the emergency stop for the machine? would save putting in a safety relay

citations.title: Using the emergency stop and external fault input correctly

tickets.answer:
No. Do not rely on the drive's STOP/RESET key or on the external fault input alone as the emergency stop for a machine.

The emergency stop for a machine must be designed from the machine's risk assessment and must follow the site's safety rules.

An emergency stop button may additionally be wired into the DI3 circuit so that the drive reports E-14 when the button is pressed. This is for indication and does not replace the machine's emergency stop circuit.

You must implement a proper emergency stop circuit that meets your site's safety requirements. The external fault input cannot be used as a substitute for this.

tickets.question_sent: Drive in cement plant panel trips on high temperature every afternoon. Heatsink looks very dusty. How often should we clean it and what is the fault telling us

citations.title: Cleaning the heatsink and air vents
E-07 Drive overtemperature (heatsink)
Meaning of the warning labels and symbols on the VX-200

tickets.answer:
The fault E-07 indicates drive overtemperature at the heatsink. Dust on the heatsink fins and in the air vents reduces cooling and leads to this fault.

You should clean the VX-200 every 6 months, or more often in dusty locations. A cement plant is a dusty location, so you should clean it more frequently than 6 months.

The fault is telling you that the heatsink is overheating. Possible causes include:
- The heatsink fins or air vents are blocked with dust (which matches what you see).
- The air temperature around the drive is too high. The drive gives its full rating from −10 °C to +40 °C and must be derated between 40 °C and 50 °C.
- The cooling fan is not running or is turning slowly.
- Mounting clearances are too small: the drive needs 100 mm of free space above and below and 50 mm on each side.
- The cabinet ventilation or filter is blocked.
- The drive is running continuously close to its rated current in a warm cabinet.

Start by cleaning the dusty heatsink. Before cleaning, let the heatsink cool: it can reach 90 °C in operation.
